'''Claudia Höbartner''' (born in 1977 in [[Krems an der Donau]]) is an [[Austria]]n-born [[chemist]]. She currently teaches as a [[professor]] at [[Julius-Maximilians-Universität Würzburg]].

== Life and work ==
Claudia Höbartner studied Technical [[Chemistry]] at [[Technische Universität Wien]]. She did her diploma thesis at [[ETH Zurich]], and after that completed her doctoral studies at [[Leopold-Franzens-Universität Innsbruck]]. In 2005, she moved to the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] in [[Urbana-Champaign]]/[[USA]] as a postdoc with an [[Erwin Schrödinger]] Research Fellowship from the [[Austrian Science Fund]]. In 2008, she became the head of a research group at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry]] (today: MPI for Multidisciplinary Science) in [[Göttingen]]. In 2014, she became a professor of chemistry at [[Georg-August Universität Göttingen|Georg-August-Universität, Göttingen]],<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2014-06-30 |title=Appointments, retirements, emeritus appointments, habilitations and rehabilitations |url=https://www.uni-goettingen.de/en/488954.html |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Georg-August Universität Göttingen |language=de-DE}}</ref> and in 2017, she succeeded Gerhard Bringmann as Professor of [[Organic chemistry|Organic Chemistry]] I at the Institute of Organic Chemistry, University of Würzburg.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. C. Höbartner - THE HÖBARTNER GROUP: ORGANIC AND BIOMOLECULAR CHEMISTRY |url=https://www.chemie.uni-wuerzburg.de/en/oc/hoebartner-group/ |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.chemie.uni-wuerzburg.de |language=en}}</ref>

== Research areas ==
Höbartner's scientific interest is in the [[nucleic acid]]s [[DNA]] and [[RNA]] and their function as [[biocatalysts]] that mediate the course of biochemical reactions. In 2016, she published the first [[X-ray]] structure of a DNA enzyme (deoxyribozyme) that catalyzes the ligation of two RNA fragments in Nature.

She has developed DNA enzymes for the detection of modified nucleotides in RNA, too.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Liaqat |first1=Anam |last2=Sednev |first2=Maksim V. |last3=Stiller |first3=Carina |last4=Höbartner |first4=Claudia |date=2021-08-23 |title=RNA-Cleaving Deoxyribozymes Differentiate Methylated Cytidine Isomers in RNA |journal=[[Angewandte Chemie International Edition]] |language=en |volume=60 |issue=35 |pages=19058–19062 |doi=10.1002/anie.202106517 |issn=1433-7851 |pmc=8457104 |pmid=34185947}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sednev |first1=Maksim V. |last2=Liaqat |first2=Anam |last3=Höbartner |first3=Claudia |date=2022-02-09 |title=High-Throughput Activity Profiling of RNA-Cleaving DNA Catalysts by Deoxyribozyme Sequencing (DZ-seq) |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jacs.1c12489 |journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]] |language=en |volume=144 |issue=5 |pages=2090–2094 |doi=10.1021/jacs.1c12489 |pmid=35081311 |s2cid=246297331 |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In 2020, she reported, also in Nature<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Scheitl |first1=Carolin P. M. |last2=Ghaem Maghami |first2=Mohammad |last3=Lenz |first3=Ann-Kathrin |last4=Höbartner |first4=Claudia |date=2020-11-26 |title=Site-specific RNA methylation by a methyltransferase ribozyme |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |language=en |volume=587 |issue=7835 |pages=663–667 |doi=10.1038/s41586-020-2854-z |pmid=33116304 |pmc=7116789 |issn=0028-0836}}</ref> the first [[methyltransferase]] [[ribozyme]] (MTR1), and published its structure and mechanism in 2022.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Scheitl |first1=Carolin P. M. |last2=Mieczkowski |first2=Mateusz |last3=Schindelin |first3=Hermann |last4=Höbartner |first4=Claudia |date=2022-03-17 |title=Structure and mechanism of the methyltransferase ribozyme MTR1 |journal=[[Nature Chemical Biology]] |language=en |volume=18 |issue=5 |pages=547–555 |doi=10.1038/s41589-022-00976-x |pmid=35301481 |pmc=7612680 |issn=1552-4450}}</ref> The discovery of the methyltransferase ribozyme provides clues to the catalytic abilities of RNA, which may have played an important role during early evolution. Methylated [[nucleotide]]s are found in the RNA of all living organisms at precisely defined sites that are essential for the structure and function of RNA. In addition, methylated nucleotides play an important role in [[mRNA vaccine]]s.

Another project of her research group deals with the investigation of the replication inhibition of  [[COVID-19]] by [[Remdesivir]] and [[Molnupiravir]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kabinger |first1=Florian |last2=Stiller |first2=Carina |last3=Schmitzová |first3=Jana |last4=Dienemann |first4=Christian |last5=Kokic |first5=Goran |last6=Hillen |first6=Hauke S. |last7=Höbartner |first7=Claudia |last8=Cramer |first8=Patrick |date=2021-09-13 |title=Mechanism of molnupiravir-induced SARS-CoV-2 mutagenesis |journal=[[Nature Structural & Molecular Biology]] |language=en |volume=28 |issue=9 |pages=740–746 |doi=10.1038/s41594-021-00651-0 |pmid=34381216 |pmc=8437801 |issn=1545-9993}}</ref>

== Academic distinctions ==
* 2004: [[Roche]] Symposium Award (Leading chemists of the next decade), Basel, Switzerland
* 2005: Georg and Christine Sosnovsky Award, (Thesis Award, Universität Innsbruck, Austria)
* 2005: Erwin Schrödinger Postdoctoral Fellowship, FWF
* 2007: [[Hertha Firnberg]] fellowship, Austrian Science Fund (FWF) & BMWF
* 2010: European Young Chemist Award ([[EuCheMS]], Silver Medal)<ref>{{Cite web |title=EuChemS Young Chemists' Award |url=https://www.euchems.eu/awards/european-young-chemists-award/ |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=EuChemS |language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2011: Research Award of the Peter and Traudl Engelhorn Foundation
* 2013: Hellmut Bredereck Foundation Award
* 2016: ERC Consolidator Grant
* Since 2019 Corresponding Member Abroad, [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] (ÖAW)
* 2020: ASEM-DUO-India Fellowship program for Professors
* 2022: Elected Member, Section Biochemie und Biophysik, [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|German National Academy of Sciences]] – Leopoldina 
* 2023: [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] (DFG)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Claudia Höbartner - Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prizewinner 2023 |url=https://www.dfg.de/en/funded-projects/prizewinners/leibniz-prize/2023/hoebartner |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.dfg.de |language=en}}</ref>
* 2023: Order of the Bavarian Constitution, Munich, Germany<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ordensträger Bayerischer Verdienstorden - 2023 |url=https://www.bayern.de/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Teilnehmer-Ordensverleihung-05.07.2023.pdf |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=www.bayern.de }}</ref>
* 2023: [[Hansen Family Award]]
